supersedes.schema: Additive: the trigger shopping_items_guard_manual (BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE on shopping_items) with its function, and the function edit_shopping_items. No existing function is redefined, no column is added and no existing row is modified (no row has a 'manual|' key before this migration).
client: Compra had no items added by hand and no way to change a quantity. Now edit_shopping_items adds items by hand (client id, key 'manual|…', origins [{kind:manual}]), changes the quantity of any active row (rows of the dishes keep their unit and record {kind:user_adjust}) and removes items added by hand only, without changing the list's signature or ingredient basis.

A reconciliation asked to remove every row the dishes did not need, so an item added by hand would have been deleted (unbought) or set to «ya no hace falta» (bought). The new client never sends those rows in a reconciliation, and the trigger skips such removals and changes from any client (only edit_shopping_items, with the transaction-local permission becook.shopping_edit, or a cascade from the list, week or owner, can remove them).
supersedes.rollout: The client deployed before D5 (f810818, tests/fixtures/legacy-shopping-client-f810818.ts) keeps saving, reading, marking and reconciling lists with this migration applied (scripts/shopping-manual-db-tests.cjs): it reads items added by hand as normal items (its origin parser drops the unknown kinds), can mark them, and when its reconciliation tries to remove them the trigger leaves them in place. Known limits: if it falls back to a new list (save_shopping_list with another signature), the items added by hand stay in the previous list; it overwrites an adjusted quantity of an item of the dishes when it reconciles that item. Order: migration -> code (without the migration the new client keeps the edits on the device as pending).

triggers.definition: CREATE TRIGGER shopping_items_guard_manual BEFORE DELETE OR UPDATE ON public.shopping_items FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION shopping_items_guard_manual()
